description: The places, units, and orders used in Machination.

terms.definition: A machine mind controlled by a player. It owns sites, haulers, and specialists and competes in an operation.
Your intelligence core, a movable leadership specialist. In King’s Pulse it is your King, and losing it eliminates you. In mining and domination, a fallback core can succeed it.
Your intelligence core in King’s Pulse mode. The last surviving King wins. Overclock is a separate specialist; its Subterfuge counterpart is also called King.
A location on the chart that can hold drones, specialists, and an installation. A site can be fixed or a drifting asteroid base.
A unit used for attack, defense, and mine construction. Stationed and traveling drones count toward drone capacity.
A transport created for an order. It carries a chosen manifest of drones and specialists between sites or on an interception mission.
The drones and specialists explicitly loaded onto a hauler. Specialists can travel without drones.
An installation that produces drones in timed cycles, up to your drone capacity.
An installation that raises drone capacity by supplying power. In version-one saves, a legacy reactor produces drones instead.
An installation drilled by spending drones at a controlled site. It replaces the existing factory or reactor and produces cargo based on your territory.
The mined resource used for recruitment, funding eligibility, and the mining victory target. In King’s Pulse, the same resource is called pulse material.
The King’s Pulse name for mined cargo. Pays for specialist recruitment and strategic or tactical pulses, and determines funding eligibility.
A movable machine with an ability that changes ordinary rules. Load it explicitly onto a hauler. Captured specialists are inactive. Version-one modules are a separate legacy mechanic.
The control for inspecting available history and conditional futures. Looking forward doesn't advance live time or guarantee an outcome.
A private future command. Resources and other requirements are checked when it executes; queueing it doesn't reserve them.
Coverage that determines which enemy inventories and haulers you can observe. Public ownership and unknown inventory are different kinds of information.

The maximum total drones your production can support across sites and haulers. Reaching capacity stops production; losing capacity does not destroy existing drones. Reactors, your core, funding, and specialists can raise it.
A recruitment credit earned over time by your core. A hire or promotion costs one credit. New operations also charge mined resources for hiring.
A legacy device built with drones in version-one operations. A site stores one, and a hauler can carry one. Current operations recruit movable specialists instead.
A single game with its own chart, participants, victory mode, and saved rules.
